questions.prompt: Two VNets are peered. A private zone is linked only to VNet A; VNet B uses Azure-provided DNS and cannot resolve its records. What is missing?

options.text: A private-zone link to VNet B.
options.explanation: Peering does not automatically add DNS-zone resolution links.

options.text: A second public NS delegation at the registrar.
options.explanation: Private-zone visibility is not set by public delegation.
That does not attach the zone to VNet B.

options.text: A public IP on every VM in VNet B.
options.explanation: Public IPs are not required for linked private-zone resolution.

questions.prompt: You link a VNet to a private zone with autoregistration disabled. What does this link provide?

options.text: Automatic registration of every VM name.
Resolution of records in the linked zone without automatic VM registration.
Public Internet resolution of the zone.
Automatic VNet peering to all other linked networks.
options.explanation: DNS links do not create network peerings.

questions.prompt: A VNet already autoregisters VM names in zone alpha.example. You want it to resolve beta.example without changing that registration. Which link is suitable?

options.text: A second autoregistration link to beta.example.
options.explanation: One VNet can have only one registration zone.

options.text: A registrar NS record for beta.example.
options.explanation: Public delegation does not provide this private link.
Multiple resolution links can coexist with the registration zone.

options.text: A CNAME at alpha.example's apex to beta.example.
options.explanation: That neither links the zone nor meets apex record constraints.
